Poorly Managed & Chaotic Restaurant -Saigon
Jan 2026 • Couples
Saigon close to district 1
Atmosphere : None - basically noisy, chaotic, staff not efficiently managed.

Although food is ok for taste, this becomes a poor dining experience, because the food is either served cold, or becomes cold waiting for sundry items like extra chappatis etc. even though we ordered in advance, explaining our expectation.

Although the our order ( all items) were discussed prior with the waiter, it was a waste of time. Execution of my order was poor and was done by several waiters who had to be called for our attention. Waiters were are headless chickens going here and there.

Our Thali, when we eat, was cold and delayed, thus negating any positive experience from dining at this restaurant.

Advice:

The owner has no clue how to manage his staff.

Suggest assigning a waiter to a table / group or an area, so that someone is held responsible and also takes on this responsibility. 
Currently it's no blame culture. The serving should arrive timely, hot and as ordered or as in a dining order. Assigned Waiter should be held responsible for ensuring this occurs.

Not really blaming the waiters, unfortunately there is no leadership at the waiting level or from the top. Totally "hands off". I have had better dining experience eating street food.

if you enjoy chaotic dining, and not too fussed how and when it is served then you are ok.

The food was very tempting
Sep 2024 • Friends
This restaurant is a divine destination for food lovers, especially for those who love south indian food. There were Idlis, Dosas with different types of Chutneys , the Tikkis and also the small vegetable wrap type . We were full by the time it reached the main course. We politely declined even to taste the Roti Dal etc. We completed our dinner with sweet Gulabjamun and/ or coconut icecream. It was a nice experience to enjoy our local food in a land far from ours. The service was really good.The owner personally verified the service in between. The food was so tempting that one of our friends ordered a take out whose husband refused to take dinner and remained in our hotel. Of course we could take only some of them due to time constraints.
